title: Laurel Creek nature centre land purchase approved
subtitle: Also: intersection safety funding, MP and MPP lease renewals, locator agreements, advisory committee review, regional joint meeting.
overview: Council approved the acquisition of 525 Beaver Creek Road, the Laurel Creek nature centre site {{vote:m12}}. It released $500,000 from the Parkland Dedication Reserve Fund and added $1,400,000 in capital funding, drawn from the Environmentally Sensitive Lands Reserve Fund and the General Contingency Reserve. This secures a nature and sports-field property for public use.

Council also released $233,000 for intersection collision review and implementation {{vote:m9}}. It gave staff delegated authority to sign dedicated locator service agreements for underground infrastructure {{vote:m3}}, and renewed City Centre leases for the local Member of Parliament {{vote:m5}} and Member of Provincial Parliament {{vote:m4}}.

Council received staff updates on the advisory committee review {{vote:m11}}, the 2025 investment report, and development charges. It supported the Mayor's nomination to the AMO Board of Directors {{vote:m8}} and agreed to join a regional all-council meeting in Cambridge on June 12, 2026 {{vote:m13}}. Presentations covered Wilfrid Laurier University's economic and social impact and the new citizen request portal.

decisions.detail: Council approved buying the Laurel Creek nature centre property, releasing $500,000 from the Parkland Dedication Reserve Fund and adding $1,400,000 in funding from two other reserves.
Council released $233,000 in 2026 non-routine capital funding for intersection collision review and implementation.
Council delegated authority to division directors to negotiate and sign dedicated locator service agreements for underground infrastructure and amended the delegation by-law schedule.
Council approved renewing the Waterloo City Centre lease for the Member of Provincial Parliament's office.
Council approved renewing the Waterloo City Centre lease for the Member of Parliament's office.
Council supported Dorothy McCabe's nomination to the AMO Board of Directors, Large Urban Caucus position, and directed the Clerk to prepare a support letter.
Council approved joining a joint meeting of regional and area municipal councils on June 12, 2026 in Cambridge.
